output.summary: KEP-378 (Kubernetes Bootstrap Checkpointing) proposed checkpointing annotated control-plane pods to the filesystem via a kubelet flag, --bootstrap-checkpoint-path, gated as Alpha. Its recorded status is implemented, stage stable, from 2020-12-29; the discussion concerns the status/stage labelling rather than the feature design.
output.rationale: The design goal was to record annotated Pods to the filesystem and have the kubelet load them on restart, to enable self-hosting. The status of "implemented" with stage "stable" was assigned retroactively during a 2021 KEP cleanup (PR #3007), which the sources say skipped PRR review. Participants disagreed on whether it should be "implemented" or "implementable", and the sources do not record a final resolution beyond the status shown.

alternatives.option: Keep the KEP at implementable/alpha without a PRR review
alternatives.why_not: The sources say the KEP was initially declared implementable at alpha before PRR was required, and a later PR retroactively declared it beta and implemented, skipping PRR.

alternatives.option: Mark the KEP as implementable (suggested by johnbelamaric for perma-beta-style items)
alternatives.why_not: The sources show this was argued in the PR discussion, but do not show it was adopted for KEP-378; the recorded status remains implemented.

evidence.quote: This KEP was initially declared implementable at alpha, before PRR was required. The retroactive PR incorrectly called this "implemented" at beta, so it skipped PRR this cycle.
It landed after https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/pull/2672 (which made PRR required for implementable), but since it landed as implemented, it skipped PRR
Given that this KEP is related to prow, and not to anything that is contained in a kubernetes release, I think this is pretty uncontroversial
The enablement of this feature is gated by a single command line flag that is passed to the kubelet on startup, ```--bootstrap-checkpoint-path``` , and will be denoted that it is ```[Alpha]```.
